question.problem:
Find the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the plane  $r=sv+tw,$ where $s,t\in R,$ and

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,w=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$
question.worked_solution:
First, notice that $v$ and $w$ are linearly independent. 

The orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ spanned by the columns of a matrix $A$ is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x=A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T}\,x.
$$

Since our plane passes through the origin, it defines the subspace $S=\text{Span}{v,w}$ in ${R}^{3}.$ In our case, we have

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ v & w \\ | & |\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ -3 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]\,⟹\,{A}^{T}=[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 & 1 \\ 2 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

 

Therefore, we get the following projection:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ -3 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot {([\begin{aligned}2 & -3 & 1 \\ 2 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ -3 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}])}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 & -3 & 1 \\ 2 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ -3 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot {[\begin{aligned}14 & 8 \\ 8 & 6\end{aligned}]}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}4 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ -3 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{10}[\begin{aligned}3 & -4 \\ -4 & 7\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}4 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ -3 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 \\ -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -3 \\ -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
